reforms.description: The federal government has announced a new fund for financing investment in green technology, aiming to spur innovation and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Additionally, the government proposes to introduce clean electricity regulations that would phase out unabated fossil fuel electricity by 2035, aiming to accelerate the decarbonisation of the electricity grid. To support this, a new Canada Growth Fund is proposed to offer 'contracts for difference' to reduce carbon cost uncertainty for firms making major green investments.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The reforms aim to stimulate investment in green technology and accelerate the transition to clean energy, which supports economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The federal government has announced a new fund and proposed regulations.
reforms.importance_rationale: The introduction of a new fund and significant regulatory changes represent major structural reforms in the energy sector.
reforms.source_quote: The federal government is proposing to use a new Canada Growth Fund to offer 'contracts for difference' as a means for reducing carbon cost uncertainty.

reforms.description: British Columbia began a two-year transition to a new royalty regime that includes a windfall mechanism, applying a price-sensitive royalty rate on revenues exceeding capital costs for development.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The transition to a new royalty regime is designed to enhance investment in resource development, which can stimulate economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: British Columbia began a two-year transition.
reforms.importance_rationale: The change in the royalty regime is significant but does not represent a complete overhaul of the system.
reforms.source_quote: In 2022, British Columbia began a two-year transition to a new royalty regime that includes a windfall mechanism.

reforms.description: Budget 2022 announced a review of the Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) Program, shifting away from tax-subsidies by lowering the small firm tax-credit rate toward the large firm rate. The savings from this move are intended to reinstate capital costs in the base for the credit and to scale up direct grants.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The review aims to enhance the effectiveness of the SR&ED program, which supports innovation and R&D activities in Canada.
reforms.importance_rationale: The review represents a significant adjustment to the existing program but does not constitute a complete overhaul.
reforms.source_quote: Budget 2022 announced a review of the SR&ED Program.

reforms.description: The federal government has initiated a major federal-provincial initiative to increase access to affordable childcare, aiming to ramp up the number of childcare spaces and reduce median costs significantly.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increasing access to affordable childcare is expected to enhance workforce participation and productivity, supporting economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The federal government has initiated the initiative.
reforms.importance_rationale: This initiative represents a significant structural change in the provision of childcare services.
reforms.source_quote: A major federal-provincial initiative is now underway that should see substantial progress towards increasing access to affordable childcare.

reforms.description: Natural Resources Canada administers a range of federal grants designed to improve the cost competitiveness of low-carbon energy generation, including a new initiative offering a refundable tax credit for solar and other energy systems.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: These grants and tax credits are intended to enhance the competitiveness of low-carbon technologies, fostering innovation and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: Natural Resources Canada administers these grants.
reforms.importance_rationale: The range of grants represents a significant but not transformative change in support for low-carbon energy.
reforms.source_quote: Natural Resources Canada administers a range of federal grants designed to improve the cost competitiveness of low-carbon energy generation.

reforms.description: The federal government is providing support for the development of charging networks to facilitate the adoption of electric vehicles, including credits and direct funding for charging station providers.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Supporting the development of charging networks is crucial for the widespread adoption of electric vehicles, which can contribute to economic growth and environmental sustainability.
reforms.status_evidence: The federal government is providing support.
reforms.importance_rationale: While important, this support does not represent a major overhaul of infrastructure policy.
reforms.source_quote: Federal government support aims to accelerate development of charging networks. CFR credits and direct funding are available for providers of charging stations.

reforms.description: The National Energy Code of Canada for Buildings (NECB) has been updated to enhance energy-efficiency standards for new buildings, aiming for net zero energy-ready buildings by 2050.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Enhancing energy-efficiency standards is expected to lead to long-term energy savings and environmental benefits, supporting economic growth.
reforms.importance_rationale: This update represents a significant structural change in building standards.
reforms.source_quote: The latest version of the code (NECB 2020) enhances previous minimum energy-efficiency standards for building envelopes, ventilation, and water and space heating systems.

reforms.description: The federal government is allocating CAD 60 million over five years to accelerate the use of climate-informed codes and standards for resilient infrastructure.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Investing in climate-informed standards is expected to enhance the resilience of infrastructure, which supports long-term economic stability and growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The federal government is allocating funds.
reforms.importance_rationale: While significant, this allocation does not represent a major overhaul of infrastructure policy.
reforms.source_quote: The federal government is allocating CAD 60 million over five years to accelerate use of 'climate-informed codes' and standards for resilient infrastructure.

reforms.description: The federal government is funding a national climate science assessment to provide new data and information about ongoing and future climate change in Canada.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Funding climate science assessments is essential for informed policy-making and can lead to better preparedness for climate impacts, supporting economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The federal government is funding the assessment.
reforms.importance_rationale: While important, this funding does not represent a major overhaul of climate science funding.
reforms.source_quote: The federal government is funding a national climate science assessment, which will provide new data and information about ongoing and future climate change in Canada.
